tail:
### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Facts block [L7] and steps citing it (1.2, 3.1)
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "[L7] Absolute value: $|t| \ge 0$, $|t| \ge t$, and $|t| = t$ for $t \ge 0$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]])."
WHY IT FAILS: The provided text of `lem-of-abs-value` does **not** contain the statement `|t| = t` for `t \ge 0`. It gives `|x| \ge 0`, `|x| = 0 \iff x = 0`, `-|x| \le x \le |x|`, `|-x| = |x|`, `|xy| = |x||y|`, and the equivalence with an interval, but not the explicit equality for non‑negative arguments. The property is true by the definition of absolute value in an ordered field, so the mathematics is unaffected, but the citation attributes to the lemma a claim it does not make.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Add a reference to the definition of absolute value (`def-abs-value`) or note that the equality follows directly from the definition. (In step 1.2 the equality is not essential; `|x_n| \ge x_n` suffices.)

### FINDING 2 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks, third bullet
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "- **Both false statements on this page have the same shape.** … The other one is [[fs-convergent-subsequence-implies-bounded]] …"
WHY IT FAILS: The page contains a single false statement (the one in the title and Statement block). The remark falsely asserts there are two false statements on the page, which is incorrect and misleading.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Remove “Both” and rephrase the remark so that it does not claim the page contains two false statements (e.g., “This false statement has the same shape as another common error: [[fs-convergent-subsequence-implies-bounded]].”)

0 fatal, 2 nonfatal
